profile.name: Zhe Jiang (Alex)
profile.intro: I’m Alex, a psychology undergraduate at ELTE. I study how the brain represents information and how those representations change with cognitive state.
profile.about: My current work brings computational analysis to fMRI and EEG research. I contribute to collaborative projects through analysis implementation, quality checks and visual reporting, alongside research team coordination.

interests.title: Neural representation
interests.description: How is information organised in the geometry of brain activity?

interests.title: Cognitive state
interests.description: How does the way we attend to information shape its neural representation?

interests.title: Computational methods
interests.description: How can careful modelling and quality control make neural data interpretable?

projects.title: The geometry of cognition
projects.summary: Relating cognitive states through the structure of neural activity patterns.
projects.question: How can the relationships between neural activity patterns help us describe cognitive states?
projects.approach: This collaborative fMRI project combines low-dimensional representations with comparisons in the original pattern space. Representational similarity analysis and pattern component modelling provide complementary ways to examine how candidate descriptions account for the data.
projects.contribution: I work on the analysis implementation, sensitivity checks and visual reporting of representational geometry, including Isomap, RSA, PCM and temporal analyses. The scientific interpretation and manuscript are collaborative work.
projects.release: High-level overview. Manuscript details and empirical results are not included in this prototype.
projects.imageAlt: Conceptual coloured point clouds representing a neural pattern space; synthetic coordinates.

projects.title: How we receive information
projects.summary: Examining neural activity across different ways of receiving sensory information.
projects.question: How do different ways of receiving information relate to brain activity and its changes over time?
projects.approach: The project examines visual and auditory information processing using fMRI. The local working materials combine activity-pattern comparisons, low-dimensional representations, state dynamics and connectivity analyses.
projects.contribution: I contribute to the computational analysis workflow, checks across analysis branches and visual research reporting. I also help coordinate the research team. Specific project roles and author lists will be reviewed before publication on this site.
projects.release: Project overview only. Internal condition definitions, results and manuscript figures are withheld.
projects.imageAlt: Conceptual state trajectories and network connections, with no empirical measurements.

projects.title: Features, perception & inference
projects.summary: Connecting measurable properties of stimuli with models of brain activity.
projects.question: How can measurable stimulus features inform models of neural responses during perception?
projects.approach: The local project includes quantitative image-feature extraction and feature-based fMRI modelling. The workflow links feature definitions, scaling and model design to first- and second-level analyses.
projects.contribution: I work with feature extraction and fMRI analysis pipelines, including implementation checks and computational workflow documentation. This is a contribution to a collaborative project; this page does not claim sole ownership of the methods.
projects.release: Methods overview only. Stimulus sets, feature tables and effect estimates are not distributed.
projects.imageAlt: An abstract stimulus marker over a feature matrix; illustrative values only.

projects.title: Making EEG analysis inspectable
projects.summary: Building an inspectable resting-state EEG workflow with human review.
projects.question: How can an EEG preprocessing workflow make each quality-control decision clear and reviewable?
projects.approach: Within the ELTE Music and Language Development Research Group, the current work focuses on resting-state EEG preprocessing in EEGLAB. It includes filtering, ICA, channel and epoch review, and documented quality-control decisions.
projects.contribution: I work on the practical preprocessing pipeline and its quality-control reports. Automated flags support manual inspection; they do not replace the reviewer’s decision. Downstream EEG findings are not presented here.
projects.release: Workflow overview only. Participant recordings, identifiers, QC records and unpublished study details are excluded.
projects.imageAlt: Synthetic EEG-like traces with a highlighted review window, not participant data.
